newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees max 10 pct Telekom sale in 1st tranche.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees max 10 pct Telekom sale in 1st tranche.

text.p: Turkish Transport Minister Omer Barutcu said a maximum 10 percent of Turk Telekom will be sold in the first tranche of the company's sell-off.

"In the first stage we will not be able to place more than 10 percent in the market. I cannot say the financial value of this," Barutcu told reporters after the constitutional court gave the green light for Telekom's sale.

He said no more could initially be placed because of the saturation of the stock market, which has risen sharply in recent weeks. A consortium headed by Goldman Sachs was last month appointed to advise on the sell-off.

The constitutional court rejected most of a challenge by 116 opposition MPs to the sell-off, opening the way for sale of the government's centrepiece privatisation and increasing hopes for other sell-offs.
The Istanbul stock market surged on the news, with the main index jumping 5.6 percent on the day in early afternoon trading.
The Islamist-led government hopes to raise $3.5 billion from the telecommunications sale, which has been halted three times by the constitutional court since 1993.
Turkey's privatisation programme has moved sluggishly since its inception 10 years ago, raising total revenues of just $3 billion despite bold government forecasts each year.
